The evidence suggests that Dofequidar acts as a target for a protein that is itself a target of a complex compound, which in turn targets the Delta-isomerase. This implies a cascading effect where Dofequidar may influence the activity of the Delta-isomerase through the intermediate protein, potentially modulating the production of isopentenyl-diphosphate, a key intermediate in the mevalonate pathway. The integration of these relationships highlights a possible regulatory mechanism where Dofequidar could influence the metabolic flux toward isopentenyl-diphosphate, though the exact nature of this interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
